{{Featured list}}
[[File:Vittorio Pozzo 1920 year.jpg|upright=0.68|thumb|right|alt=|[[Vittorio Pozzo]] is the only manager to have won the World Cup twice.]]
The [[FIFA World Cup]] is considered to be the most prestigious [[association football]] tournament in the world.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.imf.org/external/pubs/ft/fandd/2010/03/clift.htm |last=Clift |first=Jeremy |date=March 2010 |volume=47 |number=1 |title=Prize or Penalty |magazine=Finance and Development |publisher=IMF |access-date=28 September 2022 |archive-date=25 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220925201007/https://www.imf.org/external/pubs/ft/fandd/2010/03/clift.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>{{sfn|Marshall|1997|page=266}} The twenty-three World Cup tournaments have been won by eight national teams. [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] have won five times, followed by [[Germany national football team|Germany]] and [[Italy national football team|Italy]] with four titles each; [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] with three titles, [[France national football team|France]], [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] and [[Spain national football team|Spain]] with two titles each; and [[England national football team|England]] with one title.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesw/worldcup.html |title=World Cup 1930–2022 |publisher=Rec. Sport. Soccer Statistics Foundation |date=22 December 2022 |access-date=23 December 2022 |first=Karel |last=Stokkermans |archive-date=13 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221213025041/https://www.rsssf.org/tablesw/worldcup.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The role of the [[Manager (association football)|manager]] is to select the squad for the World Cup and develop the tactics of the team. Pressure is attached to the role due to the significance of winning a World Cup and the lack of day-to-day contact with players during the regular club season, aside from international breaks.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/the-set-pieces-blog/2022/jul/20/art-international-management-football-luiz-felipe-scolari-ottmar-hitzfeld-carlos-alberto-parreira-world-cup |title=The art of international football management — by those who've done it |work=The Guardian |date=20 July 2022 |access-date=25 September 2022 |first=Chris |last=Evans |archive-date=31 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221231205647/https://www.theguardian.com/football/the-set-pieces-blog/2022/jul/20/art-international-management-football-luiz-felipe-scolari-ottmar-hitzfeld-carlos-alberto-parreira-world-cup |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Alberto Suppici]] led the [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay national team]] to victory in the [[1930 FIFA World Cup|inaugural tournament]] in 1930.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/sep/23/football-fans-openly-supporting-opposite-team |title=Has a football club's fans ever openly supported their opponents? |work=The Guardian |date=23 September 2015 |access-date=25 September 2022 |first=Michael |last=Butler |archive-date=7 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221207181711/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/sep/23/football-fans-openly-supporting-opposite-team |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Vittorio Pozzo]] is the only person who has won the World Cup twice as a manager, in [[1934 FIFA World Cup|1934]] and [[1938 FIFA World Cup|1938]] with Italy.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63873325 |title=World Cup 2022: Vittorio Pozzo's legacy and a record that is finally under threat |publisher=BBC Sport |date=15 December 2022 |access-date=29 December 2022 |first=Chris |last=Evans |archive-date=15 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230315034926/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63873325 |url-status=live }}</ref> Twenty-two different managers have won the World Cup and all winning managers led their own country's national team. Six other managers finished as winners once and runners-up once; [[Helmut Schön]] (winner in [[1974 FIFA World Cup|1974]], runner-up in [[1966 FIFA World Cup|1966]]) for [[Germany national football team|West Germany]], [[Carlos Bilardo]] (winner in 1986, runner-up in 1990) for [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]], [[Franz Beckenbauer]] (winner in [[1990 FIFA World Cup|1990]], runner-up in [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986]]) for [[Germany national football team|West Germany]], [[Mário Zagallo]] (winner in [[1970 FIFA World Cup|1970]], runner-up in [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]]) for [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]], [[Didier Deschamps]] (winner in [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]], runner-up in [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]]) for [[France national football team|France]], and [[Lionel Scaloni]] (winner in [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]], runner-up in [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026]]) for [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]].<ref name=managers>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/players/3098f-coaches.html |title=World Cup 1930–2022 — Info on Coaches |publisher=Rec. Sport. Soccer Statistics Foundation |date=16 August 2018 |access-date=10 September 2022 |first1=Jaroslaw |last1=Owsianski |first2=Roberto |last2=DiMaggio |archive-date=8 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230608202234/https://www.rsssf.org/players/3098f-coaches.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2456439-deschamps-na-bereiken-wk-finale-in-illuster-rijtje-nog-een-laatste-stap-te-gaan |title=Deschamps na bereiken WK-finale in illuster rijtje: 'Nog één laatste stap te gaan' |trans-title=Deschamps after reaching the World Cup final in an illustrious row: 'One last step to go' |publisher=NOS |date=14 December 2022 |access-date=24 December 2022 |language=Dutch |archive-date=28 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528095234/https://nos.nl/artikel/2456439-deschamps-na-bereiken-wk-finale-in-illuster-rijtje-nog-een-laatste-stap-te-gaan |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Carlos Alberto Parreira]] holds the record for managing at the most FIFA World Cup final tournaments, with six appearances while in charge of five different national teams.<ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2019/06/26/carlos-alberto-parreira-international-specialist-who-never-shied-away-challenge |title=Carlos Alberto Parreira: The International Specialist Who Never Shied Away From a Challenge |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=26 June 2019 |access-date=24 December 2022 |archive-date=25 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221225072219/https://www.si.com/soccer/2019/06/26/carlos-alberto-parreira-international-specialist-who-never-shied-away-challenge |url-status=live }}</ref>{{sfn|Radnedge|2022|page=153}} Deschamps, who coached France to victory in the 2018 World Cup, has managed the most matches in the tournament at 27. He won a record 20 matches during his spell as France manager from [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]] to the [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/7/1/mbappe-deschamps-break-world-cup-records-in-sweden-thrashing |title=Mbappe, Deschamps break World Cup records in Sweden thrashing |access-date=1 July 2026 |date=1 July 2026 |publisher=Al Jazeera |last=Engineer |first=Anushe}}</ref> Suppici is the youngest manager to win the World Cup, aged 31 in 1930.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.tycsports.com/seleccion-argentina/scaloni-el-dt-campeon-del-mundo-que-le-bajo-el-precio-a-la-experiencia-en-el-futbol-moderno-id483083.html |title=Scaloni, el DT campeón del mundo que le bajó el precio a la experiencia en el fútbol modern |trans-title=Scaloni, the DT world champion who lowered the price of experience in modern football |publisher=TyC Sports |date=20 December 2022 |access-date=23 December 2022 |first=Juan Manuel |last=Collazo |language=Spanish |archive-date=16 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230516210226/https://www.tycsports.com/seleccion-argentina/scaloni-el-dt-campeon-del-mundo-que-le-bajo-el-precio-a-la-experiencia-en-el-futbol-moderno-id483083.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Zagallo and [[César Luis Menotti]] were also in their 30s when they won the World Cup; Zagallo was 38 years old in 1970 and Menotti was 39 in 1978.{{sfn|McColl|2010|p=264}} [[Luis de la Fuente (footballer, born 1961)|Luis de la Fuente]] is the oldest coach to win the World Cup, aged 65 in [[2026 FIFA World Cup|2026]].<ref> {{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/spain-coach-de-la-fuente-hails-world-class-players-2026-07-19/ |title=We are the most united team, says emotional Spain coach De la Fuente |website=Reuters |date=20 July 2026 |access-date=21 July 2026 |first=Amy |last=Tennery }}</ref>

Three men have won the tournament both as a player and as a manager; Zagallo (as a player in [[1958 FIFA World Cup|1958]] and [[1962 FIFA World Cup|1962]], as a manager in 1970), Beckenbauer (as a player in 1974, as a manager in 1990) and Deschamps (as a player in 1998, as a manager in [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]]).<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2018/07/15/world-cup-wins-manager-player-zagallo-beckenbauer-deschamps |title=Didier Deschamps Becomes Third to Win World Cup as Player and Manager |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=15 July 2018 |access-date=25 September 2022 |first=Jenna |last=West |archive-date=20 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190520130631/https://www.si.com/soccer/2018/07/15/world-cup-wins-manager-player-zagallo-beckenbauer-deschamps |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/dec/17/didier-deschamps-a-born-competitor-with-only-one-mission-in-life-to-win |title=Didier Deschamps: a born competitor with only one mission in life – to win |work=The Guardian |date=17 December 2022 |access-date=24 December 2022 |first=Philippe |last=Auclair |archive-date=14 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230614011217/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/dec/17/didier-deschamps-a-born-competitor-with-only-one-mission-in-life-to-win |url-status=live }}</ref> Both Beckenbauer and Deschamps were also the [[Captain (association football)|captain]] of their respective teams while winning the World Cup as a player.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup/didier-deschamps-france-world-cup-winning-managers-b2244336.html |title=Why isn't Didier Deschamps seen as a coaching genius? |work=The Independent |date=14 December 2022 |access-date=24 December 2022 |first=Richard |last=Jolly |archive-date=25 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221225071029/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup/didier-deschamps-france-world-cup-winning-managers-b2244336.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
